articles.title: BBC axes ‘iconic’ Ski Sunday winter sports show after nearly 50 years on TV
articles.summary: Corporation cites audience shifts and financial concerns. Broadcaster under fire for football on TV decisions. A staple of Sunday afternoon TV for almost 50 years, with an instantly recognisable theme tune, is being axed amid complaints that the BBC’s sports coverage continues to go downhill.
body: New BBC head of sport Alex Kay-Jelski has been under fire of late and will certainly not have endeared himself to some of the licence-paying public who have enjoyed the coverage of winter sports on one of Britain’s longest-running sports shows with the news on Tuesday that Ski Sunday is being dropped.

The unruffable David Vine was the first presenter of the weekly show that created household names in the UK out of alpine skiers like Franz Klammer, Konrad Bartelski and Michela Figini. While there will be no more mentions of glamorous Val-d’Isère and Val Gardena to help brighten the mood under leaden skies on a Sunday winter teatime.

Ski Sunday became equally famous for its theme tune, a rousing violin-led arrangement called Pop Looks Bach, which was composed by Sam Fonteyn and was often towards the top of polls and lists of signature TV sports melodies. It was recorded for the Boosey & Hawkes Music Library in 1970.

articles.title: Boss Goodwin leaves hospital but still absent from Dundee Utd role
articles.summary: Dundee United manager Jim Goodwin has been released from hospital after a health scare but it remains unclear when he will resume his duties.
body: Goodwin, 44, missed United's 4-0 Scottish Premiership win at Kilmarnock on Saturday after taking ill and being admitted to hospital last Thursday.
Assistant Lee Sharp took the team at Rugby Park, and will do so again for United's midweek trip to play Motherwell amid the Irishman's continued absence.
"He is out of hospital, he is back home recovering," Sharp said of Goodwin. "He is waiting on direction from the doctors etc to where he goes from there."
Asked if there was any indication when Goodwin would return, Sharp replied: "No. He would be back just now if he was allowed. We are in constant dialogue so he will let me know as soon as."

articles.title: US Open 2026: Fery, Rybakina, Fritz and Keys in action on day three – live
articles.summary: Alcaraz victorious on return | Sabalenka up and running. Alex Eala is already a global star: next up, the US Open. You can email Katy and follow us on TikTok and Bluesky. The first victory of the day goes to Comesana, who wins the toss and elects to serve first.
body: With humidity levels of 90% plus, the conditions are brutal, even with the roof on, and Comesana is already dripping so much he looks as if he’s deep into a fifth set. “I never sweated at all,” declares the Federer-like Navratilova on the commentary, “it was just my DNA.” Cobolli, meanwhile, is made to sweat as he’s pulled back from 40-0 to deuce - the Italian’s main strength, his forehand, isn’t fully firing yet – and Comesana breaks for 2-0! Having been 0-40 down in the opening game. It’s been a strange start.

Here come Cobolli and Comesana, with the Louis Armstrong roof keeping out the rain and ramping up the atmosphere. While it’s been a breakout summer for Cobolli, having reached the French Open final and Wimbledon last eight, Comesana’s had a rough 2026, winning only seven matches all year. Cobolli’s flashy, shotmaking game will likely be too much for the world No 119 from Buenos Aires today, but the Italian does have a point to prove at the US Open, having never been beyond the third round.
Away from Arthur Ashe and Louis Armstrong, it’s been confirmed that play won’t start until at least midday New York time/5pm BST.

articles.title: Aston Villa sign Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis
articles.summary: Aston Villa complete the signings of Senegal winger Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris St-Germain and English centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton.
body: Mbaye, 18, arrives from Paris St-Germain for a fee of 55m euros (£47m), while Villa could pay up to £29m for Harwood-Bellis.
Villa have paid an initial fee of £25m - with £4m in potential add-ons - for the 24-year-old defender after seeing two previous bids rejected.
Mbaye scored three goals and provided two assists in 31 games in all competitions last season as PSG successfully defended their Ligue 1 and Champions League titles.
The teenager appeared in all four of Senegal's matches at the 2026 World Cup, netting in a 3-1 defeat by France to become the youngest African player to score at a men's World Cup.

articles.title: Kevin Durant Says Some Of His Closest Friends Are 9-To-5 Workers He Met Through Video Games
articles.summary: Houston Rockets superstar Kevin Durant has been an avid gamer for years, and it turns out that hobby has led to him making some pretty special friends. During an episode of Boardroom Talks, Speedy Morman asked Durant whether he has made friends over video games and whether they know that it’s…
body: With Durant regularly speaking to this person and his group of gamers during these sessions, he decided he had to meet them in person. When he did, he realized they were great people, and they are his friends to this day. While Durant is, of course, this big superstar, some of his friends have just regular day jobs.

“We got 9-to-5s,” Durant said. “… And I’m like, ‘How y’all got so much time to play the game with me?’ My job is from 9 to 11 in the summer. I go to work, and I don’t have to do that. I just go do that ’cause I love to do it. And I’m like, ‘How y’all got so much time to play the game?’ I’m just like, man, this my safe haven for real. This is what I do to decompress.

“It’s 10 of us in a party,” Durant continued. “We competitively playing the game. We communicating, trying to win. It’s like when you think about it, it’s good for the soul when you know after a long day at work when you come home with your homies and just vibe without having to go out and have a drink or make a big production out of it.

articles.title: “A massive win” Arteta delighted Arsenal won at tough Villa Park
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta believes Arsenal’s win at Villa Park yesterday was a massive result for the team, as the Gunners demonstrated why they are the defending champions. Villa Park is one of the hardest places for any team to visit because Aston Villa have a strong team and a very good manager who knows…
body: The Villans have lost several of their best players during this transfer window, yet they still managed to field a team capable of causing Arsenal problems. They did everything possible to prevent the Gunners from finding much joy in the match, forcing Arteta’s side to work extremely hard before eventually finding a way to win.

It was not a classic performance from either team, but Arsenal will be delighted to have secured the result as they look ahead to more victories. The Gunners showed determination and resilience to claim all three points from a difficult fixture.

Arteta was delighted and relieved that his players returned from the encounter with all three points. The Spaniard also highlighted the contribution of Arsenal’s substitutes, who helped the team see out the victory.

“Really happy. A massive win. A tough place to come and earn the three points. I think we deserved it. A great squad performance, because when 11 wasn’t enough the finishers game in and did a magnificent job to finish off the game.

articles.title: Can GB and Ireland cause big Walker Cup upset and shock United States?
articles.summary: Great Britain and Ireland look to end the United States’ Walker Cup dominance and claim a famous victory on home soil this week, live on Sky Sports.
body: A sell-out crowd is expected at Lahinch Golf Club in County Clare, Ireland this weekend, where the hosts look to reclaim the prestigious trophy for the first time since 2015.
The two-day in event sees many of the world's best amateur stars compete, with Jack Nicklaus, Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy all past participants before going onto Grand Slam-winning careers.
The Walker Cup is a match play event held biennially, where the leading amateur golfers from the United States play against Great Britain and Ireland.
This year's edition from September 5-6 is the 51st in the event's history since launching in 1922, with two 10-man teams competing across 26 matches over the two days.

articles.title: Sunderland not giving up on Malick Fofana pursuit
articles.summary: Sunderland AFC are not giving up in the frantic race to sign Belgium international winger Malick Fofana (21), according to L’Equipe. The Black Cats thought they had a clean run at signing Fofana after agreeing a Deadline Day €35m for the in-demand left-winger.
body: The outlet reported that a phone call from Palace manager Pierre Sage – who oversaw Fofana’s development at Lyon – swayed the Belgian towards signing for the Selhurst Park. But there is another twist in the tale. L’Equipe now reports that Sunderland haven’t given up their pursuit of the left-sided winger. The Black Cats have reportedly revived the deal by offering much higher commissions to the player’s agents.
Furthermore, although Fofana is in London, he’s yet to undergo a medical with Crystal Palace, and the Eagles are currently left in the dark regarding the player’s whereabouts.

articles.title: Pakistan's wholesale changes 'most shocking ever', says Afridi
articles.summary: Former Pakistan captain Shahid Afridi has called the selectors' decision to make sweeping changes to the squad and remove head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed ahead of the third and final Test against England as the "most shocking ever".
body: Selectors have axed seven players, including wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, batter Imam-ul-Haq and spinner Ali Usman, after the tourists' 194-run defeat at Lord's left them 2-0 down with just one match to play, at Edgbaston from September 9.
Of the seven players to have been drafted in, five are uncapped at Test level, in Arafat Minhas, Mohammed Imran Jr, Said Baig, Mohammad Imran and Razaullah.
White-ball coach Mike Hesson will take charge following Sarfaraz's axing, while Ashley Noffke is now assistant coach after Umar Gul was also relieved of his duties.
Writing on social media platform X, Afridi said: "Not sure what is the logic or reasoning behind this decision!"
